summary: Carter Island Light, at the inner entrance to Lockeport Harbour, Nova Scotia, was first shown in 1872; the present fibreglass tower dates from 1982 or 1989.

structures.note: Square wooden tower with a wooden octagonal lantern; fixed red light (LF).
Two-storey dwelling with a square wooden lantern on its roof; LF says the buildings were demolished in 1982 except the fog-signal building.
LF dates the present tower to 1982 and gives 9.1 m; NSLPS dates it to 1989 and gives 30 ft (9.1 m); CCG list gives 11.5 m. White cylindrical tower with a red horizontal band (CCG).

access.note: NSLPS gives site access as by boat. The island is Canadian Coast Guard property.

events.note: Seventh-order lens by Chance Brothers replaced the catoptric apparatus on 7 December 1896 (LF). NSLPS dates a seventh-order dioptric lens to 1922; see resolved_conflicts.
Seventh-order dioptric lens and hand fog horn (NSLPS).
Second tower: two-storey dwelling with square wooden lantern replaced the first tower (LF; NSLPS).
Fifth-order dioptric lens, fixed red, 8 m (NSLPS).
Fibreglass tower erected; LF also says the outbuildings were demolished except the fog-signal building. NSLPS gives 1989.
NSLPS: replaced by the present fibreglass light (LF gives 1982).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1982 (Wikidata) and 1872 (Rowlett) both fit different towers: the square wooden tower was first shown in 1872 (LF; NSLPS), and the present fibreglass tower dates from 1982 (LF) or 1989 (NSLPS).

The Coast Guard list (entry 374) gives the present light as Fl W 6s, year round. The NSLPS record for the 1989 fibreglass light marks it no longer operating. The story reports both; the record is not settled here.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on the present tower's date (LF 1982; NSLPS 1989) and height (CCG 11.5 m; LF and NSLPS 9.1 m), and on the seventh-order lens (LF 1896; NSLPS 1922). LF's keeper list starts Robert McDonald in 1885; the Department's keepers' table gives an appointment date of 4 January 1886 (scan page 166). That table is OCR-aligned: the name and date are read from the same row of the same column block, and the station is matched by position, so the checker should confirm the row against the page image. The 1906-07 McDonald entry is matched by name and station on one line of an OCR list, not by date. The uncharted-rock sentence (year to June 1905) is quoted from the OCR text; its surrounding entry was not read in full. No storms, wrecks or rescues were found for this station in the sources read. A newspaper search (Chronicling America) for Lockeport in the 1880s and 1890s was not run and might add storms or rescues. Fact-check 2026-10-28: the Robert McDonald row of the 1909 keepers' table (scan 166, printed 159) was checked on the page image and reads Carter's Island | Robert McDonald | Jan. 4, 1886 on one line. The 1906-07 McDonald line (scan 152) was matched on OCR text only, not on the image. NSLPS's record for the 1989 light (no longer operating) disagrees with the Coast Guard list; the story now says so.
